---
title: Generalized decomposition R2
---

# Description

The GDR2 prior [@aguilarGeneralizedDecompositionPriors2024] is a global-local shrinkage prior that generalizes [R2D2](r2d2.html) by replacing the Dirichlet decomposition of the total explained variance with other distributions on the simplex. From this perspective the R2D2 prior is a special case, and many alternative decompositions are possible. In particular, one useful alternative is the Logistic-Normal distribution, because it allows for a flexible way to encode prior dependence between the variance proportions.

# Definition

For a linear model:

$$
\begin{align}
y_i &\sim \text{normal}(\mu_i,\sigma^2) \\
\mu_i &= \alpha + \sum_{k=1}^{K}\beta_k x_{ik}
\end{align}
$$

The GDR2 prior is:

$$
\begin{align}
\beta_k &\sim \text{normal}\left(0,\sigma^2\phi_k\tau^2\right) \\
\tau^2 &= \frac{R^2}{1-R^2} \\
R^2 &\sim \text{beta}(\mu_{R^2},\varphi_{R^2}) \\
\phi &\sim p(\nu_\phi) \\
\sigma &\sim p(\sigma) \\
\alpha &\sim p(\alpha)
\end{align}
$$

where $\phi=(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_K)$ lies on the simplex,

$$
\phi_k \geq 0,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^{K}\phi_k=1.
$$

The proportions $\phi_k$ determine how the global scale $\tau^2$ is allocated among the regression coefficients. The GDR2 framework allows different distributions for $\phi$; the Logistic-Normal distribution is the principal alternative to the Dirichlet distribution considered in the paper by @aguilarGeneralizedDecompositionPriors2024.

For a Logistic-Normal decomposition, let $\eta = (\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_{K-1})$ follow a $(K-1)$-dimensional normal distribution,

$$
\eta \sim \text{normal}_{K-1}(\mu_\phi,\Sigma_\phi),
$$

and map it onto the simplex with the additive log-ratio transform, using the $K$th component as the reference category:

$$
\phi_k =
\frac{\exp(\eta_k)}
{1+\sum_{j=1}^{K-1}\exp(\eta_j)},
\qquad k=1,\ldots,K-1,
\qquad
\phi_K = 1-\sum_{k=1}^{K-1}\phi_k.
$$

Note that $\eta$ has only $K-1$ free components. The component $\phi_K$ is fixed. This is done so that the the transform becomes one-to-one, and $\mu_\phi,\Sigma_\phi$ are uniquely determined by the distribution of $\phi$. A $K$-dimensional softmax of $K$ free normals would *not* be identifiable, since shifting all of $\eta$ by a constant leaves $\phi$ unchanged.

The mean vector $\mu_\phi$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma_\phi$ determine the prior distribution and dependence structure between the variance proportions. Setting $\mu_{\phi,k}=0$ for all $k$ means that, a priori, every proportion $\phi_k$ carries the same weight relative to the reference category, giving a symmetric prior for the variance proportions.

## Hyperparameter specification for the Logistic-Normal decomposition

Because the Logistic-Normal distribution's properties are harder to reason about analytically than the Dirichlet's, @aguilarGeneralizedDecompositionPriors2024 recommend **prior matching**: choose a symmetric Dirichlet$(a_\pi)$ with known, well-understood behavior (e.g. $a_\pi \leq 1/2$ for a decomposition that favors sparsity), then set $\mu_\phi,\Sigma_\phi$ to the Logistic-Normal distribution that minimizes the KL divergence to that Dirichlet. This has a closed form:

$$
\mu_k^{*} = 0,
\qquad
\sigma_{kk}^{*} = 2\,\varepsilon(a_\pi),
\qquad
\sigma_{kj}^{*} = \varepsilon(a_\pi) \; (k\neq j),
$$

where $\varepsilon(\cdot)$ is the trigamma function. This is referred to as the **Full KL** (or LNF) decomposition. A simpler variant drops the off-diagonal terms and keeps only the diagonal covariance $\sigma_{kk}^{*}$, referred to as **Scales KL** (or LNS). Across the paper's simulations and real-data case studies, LNS was consistently the best- or near-best-performing decomposition (in out-of-sample predictive accuracy and coefficient recovery), outperforming both the Dirichlet and the Full KL logistic-normal — so it's a reasonable default when in doubt.

For example, with $a_\pi = 0.5$ (a common sparsity-inducing choice), $\varepsilon(0.5)=\pi^2/2$, so the LNS prior reduces to independent $\eta_k \sim \text{normal}(0,\pi^2)$.

# Things to specify

Priors on $\alpha$ and $\sigma$. Hyperparameters $\mu_{R^2}$, $\varphi_{R^2}$, and $\mu_\phi,\Sigma_\phi$ (or equivalently $a_\pi$ for KL matching).

Hyperparameters $\mu_\phi$ and $\Sigma_\phi$ for the Logistic-Normal prior on the simplex. Rather than specifying these directly, it is usually easier to pick a sparsity-inducing $a_\pi$ (as in the R2D2/Dirichlet case) and derive $\mu_\phi,\Sigma_\phi$ via KL/prior matching, optionally keeping only the diagonal of $\Sigma_\phi$ (the LNS variant) for improved shrinkage and predictive performance.
